description: Composite, two-row demonstration figure (no axes, no scale bars, no numeric labels printed anywhere) showing two failure modes of MatSAM segmentation. Row (a) is headed 'Raw image', 'Expert label', 'Generated by MatSAM': the left panel is a grey-scale HRTEM micrograph of gold nanoparticles, showing several large rounded/overlapping particles with fine parallel lattice fringes plus granular noise; the centre panel is the expert binary mask, filled white particle regions on black background; the right panel is MatSAM's coloured overlay on the same HRTEM image, in which only part of one central particle and a small area of a neighbouring particle are coloured (dark green, teal), leaving most of the field unextracted, with two yellow arrows marking unsegmented regions. Row (b) is headed 'Raw image', 'Generated by MatSAM', 'Final segmentation': the left panel is an orange-brown optical micrograph of brass with equiaxed grains and straight, light-coloured elongated twin grains; the centre panel is MatSAM's pastel colour-coded pixel map (each grain a different colour); the right panel is the final binary output, black background with only white elongated twin-grain slivers as foreground. A bracketed arrow from the bottom text 'post-processing and morphological calculations needed' points at that final panel, linking the segmentation map to the filtered result.

subfigures.description: Grey-scale HRTEM micrograph of gold nanoparticles: several large overlapping rounded particles with fine parallel lattice fringes and substantial granular noise; no scale bar.
Expert label: binary mask, solid white filled particle regions against a black background, showing the correct particle boundaries.

Generated by MatSAM: the same HRTEM image overlaid with colour; only part of one central particle (dark green) and a small patch of a lower particle (teal) are coloured, two yellow arrows mark unextracted regions. Overlay semantics per-region are not fully legible.
Raw optical micrograph of brass: orange-brown etched surface with equiaxed grains and bright elongated (twin) grains; no scale bar.
Generated by MatSAM: pastel colour-coded segmentation map in which each grain/region is assigned a different colour; boundaries between grains of similar tone are hard to distinguish.
Final segmentation: binary image, black background with only white elongated needle-like twin-grain slivers retained, with a bracket/arrow linking it to the bottom annotation text.

observations.observation: Row (a) column headers read 'Raw image', 'Expert label', 'Generated by MatSAM'; row (b) column headers read 'Raw image', 'Generated by MatSAM', 'Final segmentation'.
Panel (a) raw image is an HRTEM micrograph of gold nanoparticles with visible lattice fringes inside large rounded particles.

In panel (a) 'Generated by MatSAM' only a fraction of the field is coloured (part of one central particle and a small patch below it), while the expert label fills several particles, i.e. the model output is markedly less complete than the expert mask.
Two yellow arrows are drawn on the (a) MatSAM panel pointing to regions that received no mask.
The caption states (a) is the failure example on the HRTEM image of gold nanoparticles and (b) is the process of filtering target twin grain regions on the brass micrograph.

The citing text states that on HRTEM images of gold nanoparticles the model fails to comprehensively extract multiple particles and produces severe under-segmentation due to size disparity between small atomic features and the overall region and to variations in atomic orientations within individual particles.
Panel (b) raw image is an optical micrograph of brass with equiaxed grains and elongated light-coloured twin grains, and the MatSAM map assigns a different colour to each segmented region.
The bottom annotation 'post-processing and morphological calculations needed' is connected by a bracket and arrow specifically to the (b) 'Final segmentation' panel.

The citing text states that circularity, contour geometry, area and grayscale range were calculated for each mask in (b) and that tailored filtering conditions distinguished the elongated twin grains.
The figure prints no numeric values, scale bars, axis labels or legends on any panel.

(b) middle: individual grain boundaries and colour assignments in the MatSAM colour map are partially unreadable where adjacent colours are similar
